deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a category M with arrow class Fl(M). A 'Quillen pair' (C, F) is what is now called a weak factorization system: F = C_* is the class of maps with the right lifting property against C, C is closed under retracts ('direct factors'), and every map factors as an arrow of C followed by an arrow of C_*. A 'Quillen triple' (C, F, W) is a closed model structure: C are the cofibrations, F the fibrations and W the weak equivalences, with TC = C∩W and TF = F∩W.

The page explains how to build every Quillen triple from two pieces of data, a class of cofibrations C and a class of weak equivalences W.

(a) Start with C closed under retracts.
(b) Require factorizations for (C, C_*). Then (C, TF := C_*) is a weak factorization system.
(c) Take a localizer W containing TF.
(d) Require W to be 'mildly saturated'. This means at least 2-out-of-3, which is what the proof uses; the word replaces 'saturated' crossed out on the page.
(e) Then TC = C∩W is closed under retracts. Put F = (TC)_*, which contains C_* = TF. Require factorizations for (TC, F), so (TC, F) is a weak factorization system.

Finally one must check that TF = F∩W. The inclusion TF ⊂ F∩W follows from (c). For the converse, let f: X→Y be in F∩W:
- Factor f = p·i with i ∈ C and p ∈ TF.
- Since p ∈ TF ⊂ W, 2-out-of-3 gives i ∈ W, so i ∈ C∩W = TC.
- Lift in the square formed by i and f (top arrow id_X, bottom arrow p). This gives s: X'→X with s·i = id_X and f·s = p.
- Hence f is a retract of p in the arrow category, and so lies in TF, since a class defined by a lifting property is closed under retracts.

Proposition: a pair of localizers (C, W) comes from a Quillen triple (C, F, W) if and only if:
1) C and W are closed under retracts, and W is mildly saturated;
2) factorizations exist for (C, C_*) and for (C∩W, (C∩W)_*);
3) W ⊃ C_*.

This is exactly the modern statement that a model structure is two compatible weak factorization systems plus a 2-out-of-3 class. Grothendieck then says the real work is a criterion for producing factorizations. In his cases of interest, condition 1) is free and condition 3) almost holds, apparently via the 'test' assumption, i.e. test categories. The intended application is clearly presheaf categories over test categories, with C presumably the monomorphisms and W a localizer containing the trivial fibrations. This is precisely the programme later carried out by Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006): model structures on presheaf toposes with monomorphisms as cofibrations and arbitrary accessible localizers.

ideas.what: Characterization of a closed model structure by (cofibrations, weak equivalences): two lifting/factorization systems (C, C_*) and (C∩W, (C∩W)_*), W with 2-out-of-3 and closed under retracts, and C_* ⊂ W
ideas.modern_name: Model structure = pair of compatible weak factorization systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Quillen (1967); explicit in Joyal–Tierney (2007, 'Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces'), also Hovey/Riehl expositions
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) discusses Quillen closed model categories and 'Quillen pairs'; exact formulation unsure

ideas.what: Proof that F∩W ⊂ TF via factorization, 2-out-of-3 and the retract argument
Strategy: fix cofibrations C, let any mildly saturated localizer W ⊃ C_* vary, and reduce existence of a model structure to a factorization criterion, with the 'test' hypothesis giving C_* ⊂ W
ideas.modern_name: Cisinski model structures on presheaf categories (monos as cofibrations, localizer W)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983), conjectures on test categories and modelizers carrying Quillen model structures

missed.claim: An early, explicit formulation of 'model structure determined by (C, W) = two weak factorization systems + 2-out-of-3', framed as a construction procedure parametrised by localizers W containing C_*. This is the same viewpoint as Cisinski's later theory. Mathematically standard now, but it documents that Grothendieck had the localizer-parametrised view of model structures around 1982–83.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: an antecedent of Joyal–Tierney's wfs formulation and of Cisinski's localizer theory. No new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but standard characterization of model structures; its interest is historical, as a precursor in Grothendieck's own notes of the wfs viewpoint and of Cisinski's programme, which Pursuing Stacks already anticipates.
